name: Kit Vandermeer
equipment: Camel-hair polo coat (no armor) and a hat with her press card in the band
.32 pocket pistol (Colt Pocket Hammerless, her grandfather's), 8 rounds loaded, in her handbag
Press card: San Francisco Evening Ledger, city desk
Speed Graphic camera and six flashbulbs
Evening clothes and a good suit
Engraved calling cards: Miss Katharine Vandermeer, Pacific Heights
Membership card to the Francesca Club
A nickel for the payphone in every pocket, and a roll of them in the glove box of her coupe
features: Doors Open (Old Money origin: doormen and secretaries let her through; advantage on Society checks among the wealthy; disadvantage on Streetwise until she has proved herself in a scene)
Press Pass (gets into crime scenes, press rooms and courtrooms; a source never gets burned; advantage on Persuasion to get someone to talk off the record)
The Morgue (Research takes half the time; once per long rest, one fact the paper has printed about a named person, business or address, no roll)
Ink by the Barrel (when she threatens to print what she knows about someone with a reputation, Intimidation with INT and advantage; the wrong man raises Heat by 1)
Beat: Society Page (proficiency bonus doubled on Society checks; she can get herself invited to any party, opening or benefit in the city)
Family Name (Society Heir background: the Vandermeer name opens Nob Hill drawing rooms and closes them again if she embarrasses it)

personality.traits: I talk fast, laugh loudly, and ask the question everyone else in the room was too polite to ask. I wear my grandmother's pearls to crime scenes because nobody ever throws out a girl in pearls.
personality.ideals: The people on Nob Hill have had the city to themselves for eighty years. Somebody ought to write down what they do with it.
personality.bonds: Ned Corrigan gave me my first front page, the Hotel Whitcomb jewel thefts in 1936, and never asked for a byline. My parents were at the Fairmont ball on Thursday night. So was everyone I grew up with.
personality.flaws: I would sell my own mother for a good lede, and my mother knows it, and has told her friends, which is why some of them will not speak to me.

appearance: Twenty-six, small, sharp-chinned, with bobbed chestnut hair, a camel-hair coat, a string of pearls and ink on her fingers. Her heels are always slightly too high for the hills and she climbs them anyway.
backstory: Kit Vandermeer is the younger daughter of Harold Vandermeer of the Vandermeer Shipping Line and of a mother who has been trying to marry her off since 1930. She went to a convent school in Menlo Park and to Mills College, wrote a column about debutantes for the Evening Ledger to annoy her family, and talked her way onto the city desk in 1935 by solving the jewel thefts at the Whitcomb with a tip from a private detective called Ned Corrigan, who said he did not want his name in the paper because it was bad for business. Since then she has covered fires, strikes, a bridge, two murders and the opening of the Exposition grounds, and she has kept Ned as a source, a friend and a man who bought her coffee and told her when she was wrong. Her parents are in the society-page photograph from Thursday night with Mrs. Carlton Marsh, in silver fox. She has a .32 in her handbag because Ned told her to carry one, which is exactly why Dolan has written her name down.
